root_idea.summary: The root centers on withholding, especially withholding intensified by acquisitive desire or covetous attachment.
root_idea.development: From this principle of guarded possession and eager withholding, the language extends to possessive contention, jealousy, courage as protective restraint, and persistent or vigorous application. It also yields descriptions of things that give little or resist yielding.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single QAC group represents the noun شُحّ and its related Quranic adjective/plural usage أَشِحَّةً under one lexical headword.

senses.definition: Habitual stinginess or avarice: withholding coupled with acquisitive desire.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a noun for an entrenched disposition of withholding, and in related adjective usage for those characterized by it.

senses.definition: Grudgingly withholding wealth, spoils, benefit, or aid from others; being possessively reluctant to give or assist.
senses.usage_conditions: In أَشِحَّةً عَلَى الْخَيْرِ and أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ, the plural adjective describes people who withhold material good or assistance from others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become niggardly, tenacious, stingy, penurious, or avaricious; to be covetous or greedily desirous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be construed with بِـ for being niggardly of something and with عَلَى for being niggardly toward someone or, in some usages, of something. Some descriptions distinguish it from بخل by extending it to things generally and to wealth as well as beneficence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act niggardly or tenaciously with another over something, or to be possessively tenacious of someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun مُشَاحَّةٌ is also used for reciprocal withholding, including in the making of peace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend possessively or compete over an affair, each party fearing that it will become unattainable; to press one another in seeking water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for reciprocal struggle over an object or undertaking, including two people vying for a matter or pressing toward water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of tenacious attachment or reluctance to relinquish one's condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression أَوْصَى فِي صِحَّتِهِ وَشِحَّتِهِ, it denotes the state in which a person is tenacious of, or reluctant to leave, his condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scant in yield or resistant to giving out: said of camels that yield little milk, wood that gives little or no fire, water that is small in quantity, and land that does not readily flow with water. Small watercourses are also described by this term when they are made to flow by only a skinful of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The land application is reported with opposite drainage descriptions: land requiring much rain to flow, and, in another usage, land flowing with very little rain.
This usage is explained as protective strength: one who guards what lies behind him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who applies himself persistently and assiduously to a task; by extension, penetrating, sharp, vigorous, or effective in speech or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an orator or preacher as eloquent, powerful, or skilful, and to a camel-driver who urges camels by singing. The expression for a forceful preacher is also explained through the camel's vigorous, impure roaring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A raven or crow that croaks frequently.
Light or agile, applied to an ass.
Swift in flight, applied to a قَطَاة.
Wide, applied to a desert in which stopping places are far apart and there is no herbage.
A woman resembling a man in strength, exertion, or energy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized application of the adjective to a woman characterized by unusually forceful strength or exertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Niggardly, tenacious, stingy, penurious, or avaricious; possessing little or no good.

cautions: The single Quran form group combines the noun شُحّ with related adjective/plural occurrences أَشِحَّةً; the headword is normalized to the noun while the public label preserves both parts of speech.
The land application of شِحاح is reported with opposite drainage behaviors; both are retained as reported Classical usages.
